description: Astra Pulse is a two-member team driven by curiosity, creativity and a passion for space exploration, science and technology. We aim to transform ideas into meaningful solutions by combining programming, research and problem-solving. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are exploring ways to identify Earth locations that resemble potential Moon base sites and Martian environments using scientific data and innovative technology.
summary:
Earth Analog Explorer is an interactive web application developed by Team ASTRA PULSE to explore Earth locations that may serve as environmental analogs for permanent Moon bases and Mars research.

The application integrates publicly available elevation datasets, including NASA SRTM for Earth, MOLA for Mars, and LOLA for the Moon. It provides interactive maps, terrain visualisations, elevation analysis, exploratory similarity comparisons, and candidate screening to help users investigate the characteristics of selected locations.

By bringing different scientific datasets and analysis tools together in one platform, Earth Analog Explorer makes planetary terrain information easier to explore and understand. It also highlights data availability and scientific limitations rather than presenting unsupported measurements.

Our goal is to support the exploration of potential Earth analog environments and encourage further research into planetary surface conditions.
details:
Earth Analog Explorer is an interactive web application developed to explore terrestrial environments that may provide useful comparisons for understanding the Moon and Mars. The application addresses the challenge of identifying Earth locations that resemble planetary environments and supporting further research into their surface conditions.

Built using Python and Streamlit, the platform integrates NASA planetary elevation datasets, including SRTM for Earth, MOLA for Mars, and LOLA for the Moon. It provides tools to explore four Earth analog locations, examine elevation and terrain characteristics, visualize geographical distributions, and investigate environmental similarity.

The application also includes a candidate screening feature that helps users identify the availability of scientific evidence for different research locations. It uses data processing, terrain analysis, interactive visualizations, and an exploratory similarity algorithm.

Our goal is to make planetary analog research more accessible, encourage scientific exploration, and provide a foundation for future improvements in planetary surface analysis.
